events.name: horizons
events.description: horizons was a series of 6 hackathons around the world in san francisco, sydney, berlin, singapore, toronto, and cairo! we had 50 organizers and 350 attendees across all events. 650 teens worked for over 23,000 hours on over 1,700 approved technical projects as a part of horizons.

events.name: campfire flagship
events.description: campfire flagship was a 3-day game jam in los angeles run in partnership with open sauce for 60 teens from around the world! at the event, participants were mentored by youtube creators (listed on the website) who helped them with their projects. in order to qualify, each attendee had to code for at least 60 hours on technical projects. 85 teens worked for over 6,000 hours on over 250 approved technical projects as a part of campfire flagship.

events.name: shipwrecked
events.description: shipwrecked was a 4-day hackathon on an island in the boston harbor for 110 teens from around the world! in order to qualify, each attendee had to code for at least 60 hours on technical projects. 230 teens worked for over 16,000 hours on over 800 approved technical projects as a part of shipwrecked.

events.name: counterspell
events.description: counterspell was 50 concurrent game jams all around the world! each game jam was hosted by local students in the area who we supported through the process of organzing a game jam and funded their events. across all events, we had 1,500 attendees!

events.name: hacknight
events.description: hacknight was the first hackathon i ran! it was two 36 hour hackathons at my high school - the first in 2024 and the second in 2025. the first year we had 70 attendees and the second year we had 80!

events.name: hack club satellite events - boston
events.description: i've organized the hack club satellite events in boston! we've run three of them: counterspell (game jam), scrapyard (hackathon), and daydream (game jam) at the microsoft nerd center. each one has had around 50 attendees!

projects.name: retro sdk
projects.description: a python sdk for retro's internal api + db! handles auth, media upload, albums, comments, likes, and search so you can build on top of retro without reverse engineering the api yourself.

projects.name: retro slack bot
projects.description: a slack bot that forwards photos posted to retro into slack channels! built on top of my own retro sdk - deployed on hack club's slack, it can forward posts manually or proactively dm you asking whether to share a new upload.

projects.name: nand2tetris
projects.description: my solutions to the nand2tetris problem sets, building a computer from nand gates up through an os. i published my compiler for jack on npm!.

projects.name: llp work
projects.description: trained adversarial classifiers on cifar-10 (pgd + fgsm attacks) and compared their input gradients to a pretrained diffusion model's, testing whether the two learn similar gradient patterns - a step toward one day distilling a classifier straight out of a diffusion model!

projects.name: bwsi build a cubesat challenge
projects.description: my team and i built a cubesat designed to detect power outages. i wrote the code that detects the power outages and an applet that generates synthetic power outage images.

projects.name: convolutional neural net from scratch
projects.description: i built my own cnn from scratch based on a presentation (linked above) that i gave for mit primes cs circle! right now, the underlying math works and i'm working on training it to recognize shapes.

projects.name: personal website (this website!)
projects.description: shows the projects & events i've worked on + my blog! (obviously)

projects.name: hackathon projects
projects.description: beyond running them myself, i go to a lot of hackathons! most of the projects i've built have been for various hackathons/game jams i've gone to - you can find them scattered on my github :)
